_note: Read 17 Sep 2026. Emaar's page for this building is LIVE despite the project being complete and sold out; it is titled simply 'Mulberry' and sits under Dubai Hills Estate - Emaar's own copy does not use the words 'Park Heights' on it. URL confirmed against www.emaar.com/sitemap.xml, which lists exactly three matching English property URLs: /properties/acacia, /properties/mulberry and /properties/park-heights-i. park-heights-i is a DIFFERENT building and nothing from it was used here, and nothing from the Acacia page was used here either. No agency or portal site was opened; bayut, propertyfinder, dubizzle, tanami, opr.ae, squareyards and every aggregator were excluded on principle. Emaar's 'Register Your Interest' form (name, email, phone) gates the brochure and floor plans; it was NOT filled in and nothing behind it was fetched. The page carries three project images and five shared community images. Every one was opened at full resolution and looked at - Emaar's alt text is 'Property Image 1' / 'Strapi image' and its filenames misdescribe the content, which is exactly what happened here: the file named 'property_Hero_Image' is NOT an exterior of Mulberry at all but a view out from one of its balconies, so it is recorded below with that warning and must never be used as the hero. EXCLUDED: 11016_feature_block_2_b7a4dfad86.jpg - looked at, and it is a Dubai Hills Park community scene (lawn, palm avenue, children flying kites) with only distant unidentifiable towers at the horizon; it is the community, not Mulberry, so it is not listed as an image of this building. Also excluded: the five 'attraction' images (Dubai Hills Golf Club, Dubai Hills Park, Kids' Play Area, Dubai Hills Mall, Urban Beach), which are the identical set Emaar reuses byte-for-byte on the Acacia page and across every Dubai Hills project. Net result: ONE usable exterior, and it is partial.

images.note: LOOKED: EXTERIOR, street-level / ground-level, render, daytime. BEST AVAILABLE EXTERIOR - partial. Two wings of a six-to-seven-storey apartment block with white horizontal balcony slabs and timber-toned panels, seen across the residents' pool deck and parasols from a landscaped walkway; a family and a couple of pedestrians in the foreground, planted retaining walls and lawn at the right. It is a genuine exterior of the subject building and the only one on the page, but it is a partial oblique view of two wings across the pool deck rather than a clean full elevation or aerial of the whole development, and no signage in the render names the building. 1200x779.

LOOKED: FILENAME IS WRONG - not a hero exterior. This is a view taken FROM the building, shot from a Mulberry apartment balcony: the balcony's own glass balustrade, rattan armchairs and side table fill the bottom-left foreground, and the camera looks out over Dubai Hills Park - lawns, palms, a water feature and the golf-course greens - to the Dubai skyline with Burj Khalifa on the centre horizon. A sliver of a neighbouring block's balcony flank intrudes at the right edge. Because it is shot from inside the building it is NEVER our hero and shows almost nothing of Mulberry itself. Render, not a photograph. 1620x832.
